children: Grains are starting the week with moderate gains following losses in the wake of Friday's WASDE report. Corn futures held up "pretty well" as the USDA showed larger-than-expected production and ending stocks for the U.S. and globally, Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives says in a note. "There is a near-record speculative long position in the market with U.S. harvest ramping up in the coming weeks to provide headwinds," he says. "With supplies not quite as tight as we thought, corn could see a healthy correction in the near-term." CBOT corn is up 0.2%, soybeans rise 0.2% and wheat is 0.6% higher.  (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
